headline: Superintendent outlines FY28 budget process, with a preliminary budget coming December 2nd.
summary: Three of five Budget Blitz community sessions are done. Two remain: tomorrow night at Orchard at 6:30, and a virtual session Friday morning at 9:00. The district plans more Budget Blitz weeks in January and February, and it is watching financial challenges tied to Act 170 and changes to Vermont's funding system. The board also voted to monitor equity policy 2.11, and approved four accounts payable checks over $50,000 and a Honda Odyssey minivan bid.
decisions: Approved monitoring of equity policy 2.11 using the monitoring rubric.
Approved four accounts payable checks over $50,000, including $183,686.83 to Howard Center.
Approved the bid for a Honda Odyssey minivan.
Approved the consent agenda, including accounts payable checks and the minutes for November 4th, 2026.
discussion: Budget process: The superintendent said the district does not want to simply roll over last year's budget. Budget Blitz sessions continue in January and February, and a preliminary budget comes December 2nd.

State report card results: District staff said the district ranked first in state math and third in science. Members asked which test measured college and career readiness, where the district ranked 11th.

Equity monitoring report: The report showed gaps in outcomes and discipline for historically marginalized students, and an overall compliance rating of approaching in every metric. Members questioned whether the wording of engagement surveys for young students affects the results, and whether to trim the executive limitations.
Executive limitations: Members want the executive limitations cut down and simplified, and the superintendent will review policy governance guidance on how to reconcile them.
